text:
chris: Quick follow-up from the fused-attn RFC review — a few open questions about kernel selection + graceful fallbacks. Posting micro-bench results and a suggested interface change.

maria: thanks — can you paste the perf numbers here?

chris: Sure. Short summary: fused QKV (combined GEMM + transpose) gives ~1.35x tokens/sec vs separate Q/K/V for our Llama-2-13B fp16 kernel on A100 for seq_len=1024, batch=8. Fused bias+rope variant adds another ~1.08x. Dropout-free inference path (skip dropout/seed work) negligible perf change but removes RNG state overhead.

ben: nice. Did you test with quantized kernels (4-bit/8-bit)? fusion often breaks packing layout assumptions.

chris: yes — 8-bit INT8 path maintained ~1.2x on fused QKV but 4-bit (NF4) required rework of matmul kernel; our prototype fused kernel had correctness issues (misaligned scale) so we fell back to separate Q/K/V for now.

maria: can you summarize where the runtime should decide to use fused vs unfused? I want clear policy for the scheduler.

chris: proposal: kernel_selector returns a ranked list of candidate kernels with metadata fields: {name, impl, supported_dtypes, min_seq_len, max_batch, requires_aligned_kv, quant_support}. Runtime tries top candidate, runs a lightweight correctness shim for first N batches (N=3) to validate outputs within eps, else falls back to next.

ben: lightweight shim = FP checks? how expensive is that?

chris: small: compute reference using the unfused kernel on a single micro-batch (reduced batch) and compare last-token logits L2 diff < 1e-5 for fp16, < 1e-3 for quant. We only do this on rollout or when switching kernel variants, not per-request.

dina: what about KV cache interaction? fused QKV changed memory layout in our prototype (packed QKV contiguous) — that complicates cache append/read logic.

chris: good point. Two approaches: (A) Keep same KV logical layout (separate Q and K caches) and have fused kernel internally unpack/pack; (B) adopt packed-KV in runtime and add a thin adapter layer in the cache API so older components don't notice. I prefer (A) for minimal surface area. Adapter cost = small memcpy on cache flush/restore, but fused kernel avoids extra pass during compute.

maria: adapter approach ok if we measure memory churn. For large batches the memcpy could spike. Can we make adapter zero-copy for GPU (pointer aliasing) when alignment allows?

chris: yes — adapter can detect alignment and use pointer aliasing + CUDA memmove only when needed. We'll add a flag in kernel metadata: supports_prefetch_aliasing.

ben: tying this to quantization: does packed-KV help 4-bit packing schemes?

chris: packed-KV better for 4-bit because you can store nibble-packed sequences contiguous and reduce index math inside kernel, so fused+packed is the ideal for 4-bit. But adoption requires cache format migration. That's why I favor (A) now and plan (B) as a later opt-in.

maria: operational: how do we surface failures? we need observability when kernel selection falls back.

chris: runtime will emit structured events to tracing/logging: kernel.selection.attempt, kernel.selection.success/fallback, kernel.validation.error with kernel_name, reason, sample_hash. Console will show per-route kernel health and fallback rates.

dina: tests? we need a matrix of unit + integration.

chris: proposed test matrix: unit math tests across dtypes (fp16, fp32, int8, nf4), layout tests (packed vs unpacked), KV cache read/write roundtrips, microbench harness for perf regression (95th pct), and an integration test that runs a tiny workload for 1k tokens and asserts no topk divergence over thresholds.

ben: can we add a canary rollout policy? e.g., 5% traffic to fused kernel with monitor gating.

chris: yes — runtime already has rollout slots per model-version. We'll add a kernel_tag that can be targeted in rollouts: example config:
```
model.rollout = [{version: "v2.1", kernel_tag: "fused-qkv-2026-03", traffic_pct: 5}]
```
The validation shim runs for canary and must pass before auto-promote.

maria: what's the API change you mentioned?

chris: small: the kernel selector API (internal) will return metadata as a compact JSON string per kernel. Example: `{"name":"fused_qkv_biasrope","dtypes":["fp16","nf4"],"min_seq":1,"max_seq":2048,"alias_ok":true}`. We'll add a new enum in RuntimeKernelCap: FUSED_QKV, FUSED_BIAS_ROPE, DROPOUT_FREE.

dina: backwards compatibility with third-party kernels (vendor) — how do we version capability flags?

chris: capability flags are semantic versioned. Vendors submit a manifest `kernel_manifest.json` with `schema_version` and `capabilities` list. Runtime rejects unknown schema_version unless vendor opt-in flag `allow_early_kernels=true`.

ben: one more: memory/perf tradeoff of dropout-free path — does skipping RNG reduce peak memory?

chris: small memory win: we can skip allocating RNG state buffers and some per-token temp buffers. For fp16 path on our infra that's ~2-4% VRAM saved per stream. Not huge but helpful for large-batch / long-context cases.

maria: next steps?

chris: action items: (1) infra: add kernel metadata fields + selector changes (ben), (2) eng-runtime: implement validation shim + logging (dina), (3) eng-ml: extend perf harness for NF4 fused kernels (maria), (4) docs: update rollout/console UI to show kernel tags (me). I'll open PRs and a follow-up thread with micro-bench CSVs.

ben: lgtm. pls add perf csv. :thumbsup:

dina: adding to backlog and will slot infra task.

infra-bot: Reminder: chris created ticket RNDR-4523 "kernel selector: fused-attn support + validation shim" assigned to ben, due 2026-04-02.

maria: thanks everyone — we'll sync next Tuesday to review PRs. :calendar:
